children.value: Bei der objektorientierten Programmierung und Code Factorisierung ist das Schreiben von benutzerdefinierten, neuen Modulen eine wesentliche Aufgabe. Um ein neues Modul zu schreiben, erstellen Sie zunächst ein neues Skript. Dann öffnen Sie das neue Skript und fügen Sie einige Parameter und Funktionen hinzu.

# icecreamdialogue.py
flavors = ["vanilla", "chocolate", "bread"]
price_scoops = {1: "two euros", 2: "three euros", 3: "your health"}
welcome_msg = "Hi, I only have " + flavors[0] + ". How many scoops do you want?"
can now either be executed as a script (nothing will happen visibly) or imported as a module to access its variables (e.g.,

import icecreamdialogue as icd
print(icd.welcome_msg)
scoops_wanted = 2
print("That makes {0} please".format(icd.price_scoops[scoops_wanted]))
As an alternative, we can append the call to items in
in the script and run it as a stand-alone script by adding an

# icecreamdialogue_standalone.py
flavors = ["vanilla", "chocolate", "bread"]
price_scoops = {1: "two euros", 2: "three euros", 3: "your health"}
welcome_msg = "Hi, I only have " + flavors[0] + ". How many scoops do you want?"


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(welcome_msg)
    scoops_wanted = 2
    print("That makes {0} please".format(price_scoops[scoops_wanted]))
